The entirety of War and Peace is about the Napoleonic Wars and I believe in the context Tolstoy was talking about the greater historical context that affect the choices that a leader is presented with.

Basically a leader is dealt a hand by the context of the circumstances that lead him to power but he still has free range of what to do with circumstances. I don't believe Tolstoy was positing a pseudo-Calvinist doctrine of predetermination but rather was saying that a leader is like a character in a Greek tragedy always subjugated to things beyond his control.

In the context of the book I believe Tolstoy was particularly referencing Napoleon and the French Revolution which allowed him to rise power. It does contrast with the Great Man Theory insofar as it says a man is byproduct of his times rather than the times being the byproduct of a singular great man.
